questions.question: Which Veda depicts the information about the most ancient Vedic age culture?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Rig Veda__**

**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The Rig-Veda is the oldest of the four collections of hymns and other sacred texts known as the Vedas.
 
• It contains most of the information about the religious and social life of the early Vedic period.
 
• These works are considered the "sacred knowledge" of the Aryans.
 
• The Rig-Veda also contains ideas that served as the basis for India's system of castes(Varna).
 
• According to Brahminic ideology, Varṇa means hierarchizing society into classes.

questions.question: What was the other name of Chanakya?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2 i.e __**Vishnugupta**__

__
 
• **Vishnugupta**__ was the other name of **Chanakya**.
 
• He was born around **350 BC** and is known for his being the chief architect of the Mauryan empire and writing the pioneering work in the Economics and Political Science that is **Arthashastra**.
 
• Chanakya was identified with Vishnugupta in a verse in his Arthashastra and also in Panchatantra of Gupta age by Vishnu Sharma.
 
• Vishakhadatta was an Indian Sanskrit poet and playwright. 
 
• He wrote political drama **Mudraraksasa**.

questions.question: What are sea waves generated by undersea earthquakes called?
questions.solution: A tsunami is a series of ocean waves caused by an underwater earthquake, landslide, or volcanic eruption.

questions.question: Constitution of India was enforced on ________.
questions.solution:
• Constitution of India which was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 26th November 1949 and enforced into force on 26th January 1950.
 
• The Constituent Assembly, which first met on December 9, 1946, took precisely 2 years, 11 months and 18 days to come up with the final draft of the Indian Constitution.

questions.question: The process of amendment has been mentioned in which part of the Indian Constitution?
questions.solution:
• Article 368 in part 20 of the Constitution deals with powers of Parliament to amend the Constitution and its procedure.
 
• It states that the Parliament may, in the exercise of its constituent power, amend by way of addition, variation or repeal any provision of the Constitution in accordance with the procedure laid down for the purpose.
 
• Parliament cannot amend those provision that comes under The Basic structure of the Constitution. The basic structure was given by the Supreme Court in the famous Kesvanand Bharti Case of 1973.

questions.question: The state of economy at which the value of the currency falls and the price increases, is called ________.
questions.solution:
• **Inflation **is the state in any economy when prices of goods and services increase due to demand and supply and other prospects.
 
• Inflation is a sustained increase in the general price level of goods and services in an economy over a period.
 
• It says the primary cause of inflation is the printing out of too much money by the government. As a result, too much capital chases too few goods.

 
 

 
 
Inflation

 
 
 
It is a sustained increase in the general price level of goods and Services.

 
 
 

 
 
Retail inflation

 
 
 
Measured in term of CPI(Consumer Price Index)

 
 
 

 
 
Wholesale inflation

 
 
 
Measured in term of WPI(wholesale price index)

 
 
 

 
 
Outcome of Inflation

 
 
 
 
• Inflation provides benefits to debtors and loss to creditors/bondholders.
 
• Limited inflation is good for growth in developing countries.
 
 
 
 

 
 
Consumer Price Index (CPI)

 
 
 
A measure that examines the weighted average of prices of a basket of consumer goods and services, such as transportation, food, and medical care.

questions.question: The difference between isotopes of an element is due to the presence of which different numbers?
questions.solution:
• Isotopes have different mass numbers, though, because they have different numbers of neutrons.
 
• Isotopes are atoms with the same number of protons but that have a different number of neutrons.
 
• Since the atomic number is equal to the number of protons and the atomic mass is the sum of protons and neutrons, we can also say that isotopes are elements with the same atomic number but different mass numbers.

questions.question: Working principle of washing machine is _________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Centrifugation.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__ **

__
 
• **Washing machine**__ works on the principle called __**Centrifugation.**__
 
• Centrifugation is a separation process which uses the action of centrifugal force to promote accelerated settling of particles in a solid-liquid mixture.

questions.question: Which is the smallest flower in the world?
questions.solution:
• The world’s smallest flowering plant is the Wolffia globosa.
 
• Wolffia is the smallest genus of the aquatic plants known as duckweeds, which are part of the family Lemnaceae.
 
• It is found floating in masses in freshwater lakes, streams, and marshes throughout the world.

questions.question: Who discovered the nucleus for the first time in cell?
questions.solution:
• Nucleus of a cell was discovered by Robert Brown in 1831.
 
• He is perhaps best known for his discovery of the random movement of microscopic particles in a surrounding solution, later referred to as Brownian motion.
 
• Nucleus of an atom was discovered by Ernest Rutherford's.

questions.question: Muscle study is called ________.
questions.solution:
• Myology is called the Study of muscles.
 
• Myology is the science that studies muscles, their physical structure, type of fibers, specific function, and the connections between different muscle groups.
 
• Myology was considered as a little part of Neurology, while currently it is recognized as an autonomous discipline both at the research and the medical level.

questions.question: An example of abiotic component of the environment is ________.
questions.solution:
• Wind is an example of abiotic component of environment.
 
• Abiotic components or abiotic factors are non-living chemical and physical parts of the environment that affect living organisms and the functioning of ecosystems.
 
• These are also called as the ecological factors.
 
• The physical and chemical factors are characteristic of the environment. Light, air, soil, and nutrients etc. form the abiotic components of an ecosystem.

questions.question: Which of the following is considered as the fastest printer?
questions.solution:
• Laser printer is known to be the fastest printer.
 
• It is a type of printer linked to a computer producing good-quality printed material by using a laser to form a pattern of electrostatically charged dots on a light-sensitive drum, which ink powder.
 
• The ink is transferred to a piece of paper and fixed by a heating process.

questions.question: Who is the exponent of Quantum theory?
questions.solution:
• Max Planck was a German theoretical physicist, considered to be the initial founder of Quantum theory.
 
• That light and other electromagnetic wave were emitted in discrete packets of energy that he called quantum in the singular which could only take on certain discrete values (multiples of a certain constant, which now bears the name the “Planck Constant”).

questions.question: Which kind of instrument is Mridangam?
questions.solution:
• Mridangam is a two-faced drum used in south Indian music.
 
• Mridangam is the main percussion instrument of the South Indian or Carnatic form of music and is used to accompany vocalists and all types of melodic instruments of South India.
 
• Percussion instruments include any instrument that makes a sound when it is hit, shaken, or scraped.
 
• It is also used as an accompaniment for Bharatanatyam and other forms of Indian dance.

questions.question: When does Bangladesh celebrate its Independence Day?
questions.solution:
• The Independence Day of Bangladesh is celebrated on 26 March 1971.
 
• It commemorates the country's declaration of independence from Pakistan in the late hours of 25 March 1971.

questions.question: Which of the following country's government passed the "Hindu Marriage Bill 2016"?
questions.solution:
• Pakistan's Government passed the 'Hindu Marriage Bill 2016'.
 
• The bill will help Hindu women get documentary proof of their marriage.
 
• It is the first personal law for Pakistani Hindus, applicable in Punjab, Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa provinces.
